step_by_step_reasoning: The whiteboard shows the Levels Beyond Media to Cloud workflow. Nodes: web user (entry point), S3, Step Functions, MediaConvert, Rekognition, Transcribe, Comprehend, DynamoDB, EC2 and EKS (both hosting Reach Engine; kept as separate nodes since they are distinct services drawn separately). Lambdas are mentioned in audio but not drawn and not in the inventory; they are assimilated into the Step Functions -> DynamoDB edge notes. The ledger has 14 visual_connections entries; I emit 14 edges, one per entry, with the same source and target, including both directions StepFunctions<->MediaConvert and Transcribe<->DynamoDB. Flow 0: upload and transcode plus technical metadata. Flow 1: Rekognition analysis. Flow 2: Transcribe and Comprehend analysis. Flow 3: ingest from DynamoDB into Reach Engine (EC2/EKS). The DynamoDB -> Transcribe edge is not described in audio, so it is emitted as data with an empty note.

graph.name: Levels Beyond: Media to Cloud Workflow with Reach Engine
graph.notes: Media to Cloud workflow: users upload video to S3, Step Functions orchestrates MediaConvert proxy transcoding, technical metadata extraction, Rekognition, Transcribe and Comprehend analysis; results are stored temporarily in DynamoDB and then ingested into Reach Engine running on EC2 and EKS.

nodes.name: User
nodes.notes: User uploads media files (any video format) and later plays back proxies in the browser.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Bucket receiving user uploaded video files; upload triggers the workflow.

nodes.name: Step Functions
nodes.notes: Orchestrates video processing flows: kicks off transcode, triggers Lambdas to extract checksums and technical metadata, then triggers a further step function for Rekognition and Transcribe.

nodes.name: Elemental MediaConvert
nodes.notes: Transcodes video to create a proxy suitable for playback in the browser, giving users a visual check alongside the extracted metadata.

nodes.name: Rekognition
nodes.notes: Analyzes video to identify celebrities, violence, nudity and other data; results are associated with time codes.

nodes.name: Transcribe
nodes.notes: Converts the audio of the content into text.

nodes.name: Comprehend
nodes.notes: Analyzes the transcribed text to extract entities and detect things like profanity.

nodes.name: DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Temporary data store for video metadata (checksums, frame rates, media info, highlights with time codes, transcription and text analysis) before ingest into Reach Engine.

nodes.name: EC2 (Reach Engine)
nodes.notes: Hosts Reach Engine, the core product: content playback, metadata viewing and search, visualization of celebrity tracks, and an orchestration engine to distribute content for monetization.

nodes.name: EKS (Reach Engine)
nodes.notes: Hosts Reach Engine, the core product: content playback, metadata viewing and search, visualization of celebrity tracks, and an orchestration engine to distribute content for monetization.

edges.notes: User uploads a media file to the S3 bucket.
The upload triggers a step function.
Step function kicks off the transcode in MediaConvert to create a browser playback proxy.
Proxy generation completes and the step function continues.
Step function triggers Lambdas that extract checksums and standard technical metadata (frame rates, media info) and store it in DynamoDB.
After basic metadata extraction, another step function is triggered that starts Rekognition on the video.
Detected celebrities, violence, nudity and other data, associated with time codes, are stored in DynamoDB.
The same step function triggers Transcribe to convert the audio into text.
Transcribed text is sent to Comprehend for analysis.
Transcription output is stored in DynamoDB.
Extracted entities and text analysis (e.g., profanity occurrences) are stored in DynamoDB.
Once the data is in DynamoDB, an ingest into Reach Engine is triggered.
Once the data is in DynamoDB, an ingest into Reach Engine is triggered.
